slot.brief: Three/four point masses placed at corners of a square or along a rod; find coordinates of centre of mass by weighted average (simple direct computation).

stem: Four point masses are placed at the corners of a square of side $2\ \text{m}$. Their coordinates and masses are $(0,0):1\ \text{kg}$, $(2,0):2\ \text{kg}$, $(0,2):3\ \text{kg}$ and $(2,2):4\ \text{kg}$. The centre of mass has coordinates

verdicts.working: Total mass = 10 kg. The weighted coordinates are x = (2×2 + 4×2)/10 = 1.2 m and y = (3×2 + 4×2)/10 = 1.4 m.

working:
$M=1+2+3+4=10\ \text{kg}$
$x_{\rm cm}=\dfrac{1(0)+2(2)+3(0)+4(2)}{10}=1.2\ \text{m}$
$y_{\rm cm}=\dfrac{1(0)+2(0)+3(2)+4(2)}{10}=1.4\ \text{m}$

Independent check: Total mass = 10 kg. The weighted coordinates are x = (2×2 + 4×2)/10 = 1.2 m and y = (3×2 + 4×2)/10 = 1.4 m.
solution:
For point masses, $x_{\rm cm}=\dfrac{\sum m_i x_i}{\sum m_i}$ and $y_{\rm cm}=\dfrac{\sum m_i y_i}{\sum m_i}$. With total mass $M=10\,\text{kg}$,
$$x_{\rm cm}=\dfrac{2(2)+4(2)}{10}=1.2\,\text{m},\qquad y_{\rm cm}=\dfrac{3(2)+4(2)}{10}=1.4\,\text{m}.$$
Hence, the centre of mass is $(1.2\,\text{m},\ 1.4\,\text{m})$.
